title: Wear OS Surfaces, Power, and Health Context Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies wear os surfaces, power, and health context?
options: Choose wrist-appropriate surfaces, keep tasks focused, minimise power and data, and preserve standalone and offline behavior.
questions.answer: Choose wrist-appropriate surfaces, keep tasks focused, minimise power and data, and preserve standalone and offline behavior.
questions.explanation: The correct response preserves authority, compatibility, exact artifact evidence, adverse-path behavior, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: A full-screen Wear app is the preferred surface for every piece of frequently checked information.
questions.explanation: Porting the complete phone information architecture to a watch creates deep, slow interactions that fight wrist ergonomics and battery constraints.

questions.prompt: When is a complication preferable to a full app?
questions.answer: For a tiny frequently glanced value or action that users need directly on the watch face.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the contract or mechanism that remains valid beyond one implementation demonstration.
